identity.title: ALMA High Angular Resolution Polarization Study: An Extremely Young Class 0 Source, OMC-3/MMS 6

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using the $\approx$15km ALMA long baselines, we imaged the Stokes $I$ emission and linearly polarized intensity ($PI$) in the 1.1-mm continuum band of a very young intermediate-mass protostellar source

question.value: What is the origin of the 1.1 mm dust polarization (magnetic alignment, self-scattering, or anisotropic radiation) in the central 200 AU of the Class 0 protostar MMS 6, and how does it compare with MHD simulations?

evidence.quote: The new ALMA data allow us to study the polarization and magnetic field structures at the center of a protostellar core, MMS 6/OMC-3 at the highest angular resolution as possible with current ALMA
The ALMA observations of MMS 6 were obtained through the science project 2015.1.00341.S (P.I. S. Takahashi)

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate and image Stokes I, Q, U

method.value: Standard observatory scripts in CASA 4.5.0; clean with Briggs robust 0.5 (high res) and natural (low res); self-cal for low res

evidence.quote: The Briggs weighting with robust parameter of 0.5, and natural weighting were used for the high and low angular resolution final images, respectively.

key_parameters.value: Polarization calibrator J0522-3627 observed every 25 minutes

evidence.quote: removing instrumental polarization using a bright polarized calibrator, J0522-3627, which was observed every 25 minutes during each execution

validation.value: Q and U rms near thermal noise; Stokes I dynamic-range limited

evidence.quote: The Stokes $Q$ and $U$ image rms is near the expected thermal noise level.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive PI, E-vector angle and polarization fraction

method.value: PI=sqrt(Q^2+U^2) with 5 sigma debiasing; EPA=0.5 arctan(U/Q); Dfrac=PI/I using pixels with PI>5 sigma and I>3 sigma

evidence.quote: only those pixels that contain both more than 5$\sigma$ signal level in the $PI$ maps and 3$\sigma$ signal level in the Stokes $I$ maps, were used for calculating $D_{\rm frac}$

key_parameters.value: Delta PI = sqrt(dQ^2+dU^2+(0.002 I)^2); lower limit of Delta EPA about 1 deg

evidence.quote: There is a lower limit of $\Delta E_{PA}$ of $\approx 1^\circ$

validation.value: Compared high and low resolution images: 96% Stokes I flux recovered in central 0.5 arcsec

evidence.quote: we are recovering 96% of Stokes $I$ flux in the central 200 AU

analysis_steps.goal: Fit Stokes I structure with multiple Gaussians and estimate physical properties

method.value: 2D three-component Gaussian fit; masses, column and number densities derived from fluxes assuming tau~1

evidence.quote: we used a two-dimensional Gaussian fit with multiple components

key_parameters.value: Mean dust temperatures 25, 27, 36 K; beta=0.93; kappa(1.1mm)=0.014 cm2/g

evidence.quote: Assuming the respective mean dust temperatures of 25, 27, and 36 K for the extended, elongated, and compact components, an optical depth of ${\tau}{\approx}1$, a gas-to-dust ratio of 100

assumptions.value: Gas-to-dust ratio 100, tau≈1, spherical geometry for densities, distance 414 pc

evidence.quote: A spherical geometry with the geometric mean of the major and minor axes of the source size is assumed in order to estimate the number densities.
The residual level of the fitting result is less than 1.5% with respect to the observed peak flux

validation.value: Compared with SMA mass from earlier work

evidence.quote: the estimated mass would be agreement within a factor of 1.3

method.value: Qualitative comparison of observed characteristics with magnetic alignment, self-scattering, anisotropic radiation predictions (Table 4)

evidence.quote: Table 4 summarizes how each of the characteristics could fit in each proposed polarization mechanism.

method.value: Simulated projected polarization map at viewing angle 60 deg, optically thin, compared qualitatively with ALMA maps

evidence.quote: Optically thin condition was assumed when making this projection. A viewing angle of $i$=60$^{\circ}$ was used

key_parameters.value: Bonnor-Ebert core, n_c=2e5 cm-3, T=10 K, B0=26 uG, Omega0=1e-13 s-1, Mcore=8.7 Msun, finest cell 0.2 AU

evidence.quote: The cell size of the finest grid is 0.2 AU.

assumptions.value: Viewing angle chosen so outflow lobes do not overlap and best fits Figure 5(c)

evidence.quote: Also the inclination angle of 60$^{\circ}$ appears to be a better fit to explain our observed results

used_for.value: Calibration, clean imaging, immath for PI/EPA, immoment for velocity maps

evidence.quote: The Common Astronomy Software Application (CASA; (cite: 2007ASPC..376..127M)) version 4.5.0 was used for the standard ALMA data reduction.

findings_qualitative.value: Ring-like polarized structure (~80 AU radius) seen in PI but not Stokes I, with a depolarization gap and ~90-105 deg change in E-vector P.A.

evidence.quote: A partial ring-like structure with a radius of $\approx$80 AU is detected in $PI$ but not in the Stokes $I$.

claims.hypothesis: Self-scattering alone explains the central polarization
claims.experiment: Compare observed pattern, offset and degree with self-scattering models
claims.result: Pattern and offset consistent; degree 11% too high
claims.finding: Self-scattering cannot explain high polarization degree

evidence.quote: this model is not able to reproduce the observed high degree of polarization

claims.hypothesis: Toroidal wrapping of magnetic field explains ring and arm structures
claims.experiment: Projected polarization from 3D non-ideal MHD simulation at i=60 deg
claims.result: Ring-like and arm-like structures reproduced; central 50 AU not reproduced
claims.finding: Magnetic alignment best explains observations, with limits near center

evidence.quote: The simulations are consistent with the $PI$ emission in the ring-like and the extended arm-like structures observed with ALMA.

claims.hypothesis: Anisotropic radiation alignment explains the polarization
claims.experiment: Compare E-vector orientation with azimuthal prediction
claims.result: Ring not centered on source; central vectors not pointing to protostar

evidence.quote: Our observational results, therefore, cannot unambiguously support this scenario.

why_this_data.value: MMS 6 is bright and relatively close, a unique target for highest-resolution polarization

evidence.quote: MMS 6 is a bright source and relatively close, so it is a unique target to observe the polarized emission at the ALMA highest angular resolutions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gold (1952) mechanical alignment parallel to flow rejected; E-vectors perpendicular to outflow cavity

evidence.quote: The observational result does not support the scenario expected by (cite: 1952MNRAS.112..215G)

limitations_admitted.value: MHD simulation with sink cell cannot resolve central region or include protostar radiation

evidence.quote: Thus, we cannot resolve the central region or protostar itself.

limitations_admitted.value: About 25% Stokes I flux missing in central 2 arcsec, so Dfrac in extended structure may be overestimated

evidence.quote: for the central $2''.0$, comparison with low resolution maps suggests that about 25% is missing in the Stokes $I$ emission

referee_caveats_inferred: Stokes I is dynamic-range limited, affecting Dfrac
Mechanism comparison is qualitative; no quantitative scattering or radiative-transfer model fit
MHD viewing angle chosen by fit to data
Dust temperatures and tau~1 make mass estimates lower limits
Typo-level inconsistencies in beam and weighting descriptions between text and Table 1

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA project 2015.1.00341.S acknowledged; public status not stated

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2015.1.00341.S.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~100-300 GB raw for the long-baseline and compact-array continuum polarization datasets
reproducibility.score_reason: Observational recipe is mostly clear (CASA 4.5.0, robust 0.5, formulae for PI), but clean/selfcal details missing and MHD comparison is not reproducible.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results are partly numeric, but polarization calibration and imaging specifics are incomplete and the interpretation is qualitative.
